## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Reviewer identities are hidden from authors, from other reviewers and from editors not handling the paper; the pages do not say whether author identities are hidden from reviewers. After all reviews arrive, the handling editor generally sends the anonymised reviews to all reviewers (https://jair.org/index.php/jair/about/submissions; retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Blank. No transfer scheme on the pages read |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Blank. The journal publishes aggregate submission statistics, not reports (https://jair.org/index.php/jair/transparent-publishing) |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | The journal does not accept papers subject to major revision: such papers are rejected with encouragement to resubmit, normally to the same associate editor and reviewers, and a paper may be resubmitted at most once. For papers accepted with minor revisions, authors normally have up to two months. The published figure for resubmissions: a revised version resubmitted on 2026-01-02 (six weeks after a first decision) would have been accepted by 2026-04-21 with probability 67.3% (https://jair.org/index.php/jair/transparent-publishing and the submissions page). For special tracks the page states at most two rounds of reviewing (https://jair.org/index.php/jair/about) |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Reviewers recommend accept, accept with minor revisions, reject with resubmission encouraged, or reject (https://jair.org/index.php/jair/about/submissions; retrieved 2026-11-23) |

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | Yes, a short journal-specific paragraph on the submissions page |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | No gate. The page states no mandatory disclosure statement |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 4 (assistance with editing, language, idea generation and data analysis is allowed; no disclosure form is required on the page read; the core contributions must come from the authors) |
| **Summary** | Authors are fully responsible for originality, accuracy and integrity. AI tools, including large language models, may assist with editing, language, generating ideas or analysing data. AI cannot be credited as an author or cited as an independent source. Any AI use in the paper, references or metadata should be carefully reviewed for accuracy and attribution. Source: https://jair.org/index.php/jair/about/submissions, retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Source URL** | https://jair.org/index.php/jair/about/submissions |

> Source: https://jair.org/index.php/jair/about/submissions and https://jair.org/index.php/jair/faq (retrieved 2026-11-23). Posting a preprint before or during review is not addressed on the pages read; the submission declaration says the manuscript must not be under review or published elsewhere, with an exception for extended versions of conference papers.

| Stage | Allowed? | Notes |

| Pre-submission | Blank | Not addressed on the pages read |

| Version of Record | Yes | All articles are open access; articles published on or after 2023-05-01 are under CC BY, earlier ones (volumes 1 to 76) under the JAIR License Version 1 (https://jair.org/index.php/jair/about) |

## Format

> Source: https://jair.org/index.php/jair/about/submissions, https://jair.org/index.php/jair/formatting, https://jair.org/index.php/jair/authorinstrs and https://jair.org/index.php/jair/about, all read live on 2026-11-23.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Full-length research articles, research notes (very brief papers extending or evaluating previous work), survey articles and special-track articles. The about page says survey submissions are paused from 2026-12-01, with reopening planned for January 2027. OpenAlex type counts, 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23: 587 articles, 5 reviews (retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Word limit** | No word or page limit found on the pages read. The editorial charter says short, high-quality articles are welcome and authors are urged to be concise (https://jair.org/index.php/jair/about) |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Not applicable: no limit found |
| **Abstract limit** | No word count found. Structured abstracts (Background and further labelled parts) are encouraged but not mandatory, through the journal's LaTeX template (submissions page). 41 of the 592 OpenAlex abstracts begin with "Background" (pattern `structured_abstract` in AI-Research Notes): 31 dated 2026, 9 dated 2025, 1 dated 2024 |
| **Reference limit** | No cap found |
| **Supplementary material** | Online appendices (data, demonstrations, source code) are welcome and are not included in the review; appendices with source code need a signed release form (submissions page and https://jair.org/index.php/jair/authorinstrs) |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit found. Colour is welcome, but figures must be understandable in monochrome, and referees may not see the colour version (submissions page) |
| **Style / submission format** | PDF only, in the JAIR format; since spring 2025 the format is an ACM-based LaTeX style (https://jair.org/index.php/jair/formatting); submissions in another format, for example a conference format, are rejected without review; a completed reproducibility checklist from the template must be appended, and submissions without it are desk rejected; three answers (150 words or fewer each) are required in the submission comments, including 1 to 3 closest JAIR papers; no copyediting staff, so authors proofread |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes, stated by the journal: the manuscript must describe new methods, results or insights important to the global AI community or a well-established sub-community, with claims supported by empirical evidence or theoretical analysis (https://jair.org/index.php/jair/about/submissions; editorial charter at https://jair.org/index.php/jair/about). Retrieved 2026-11-23.
- **What kind of engagement?** Papers should report what was learned rather than what was done, acknowledge predecessors, and say why current terminology is insufficient if new terms are introduced; theory papers should also discuss practical utility; reported experiments should be reproducible (editorial charter).
- **Required submission answers**: the submission form requires three answers, namely why the work matters to other AI researchers (150 words or fewer), 1 to 3 closest JAIR papers and how the work differs (150 words or fewer), and any prior or parallel publication; articles with little similarity to published JAIR articles have a high chance of rejection without review (https://jair.org/index.php/jair/about/submissions).
- **Categories the journal says usually face summary rejection**: papers rejected elsewhere without extensive improvement; incremental or narrow-audience results; surveys that only summarise literature; papers that apply known AI techniques without methodological insight; papers insufficiently grounded in the state of the art (submissions page).
- **Article types**: research articles, research notes, surveys (paused from 2026-12-01, reopening planned January 2027) and special tracks (about page).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: the journal states that a significant fraction of first-time submissions are summarily rejected, often for lacking results of importance to the global AI community or methodological insight (https://jair.org/index.php/jair/transparent-publishing); no desk-reject percentage is stated.

Scoring convention of this research pass (its own, not an external standard): share 0 = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement, and none was found. | **Data transparency requirement** | A reproducibility checklist is mandatory: it is appended to the submission, and submissions without it are desk rejected; reported experiments should be reproducible; online appendices for data and code are encouraged but are not reviewed (https://jair.org/index.php/jair/about/submissions; retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Reviewer identities are hidden from authors; the pages do not say whether author names are hidden from reviewers. Preprints during review are not addressed on the pages read (Preprint Policy) |
| **AI use** | AI assistance allowed for editing, language, ideas and data analysis; AI is not an author; no disclosure form stated (https://jair.org/index.php/jair/about/submissions) |
| **Open access and cost** | Diamond open access; no submission or publication fee; CC BY from 2023-05-01 (https://jair.org/index.php/jair/about) |
| **Duplicate submission** | A manuscript under review or published elsewhere is rejected and the authors are banned from submitting to the journal for six months; extended versions of conference papers are allowed if declared (https://jair.org/index.php/jair/about/submissions) |
| **Authorship changes** | After acceptance, authorship cannot change without explicit permission from the editors-in-chief (https://jair.org/index.php/jair/about/submissions) |

**Method note:** OpenAlex was used sparingly (4 direct requests: a sources lookup and 3 paged downloads of up to 200 records, plus the import script's own) without any key or email and without HTTP 429. Keyword shares were counted locally from the downloaded records, so every share has an exact pattern; the masthead roles were counted from the page's HTML (one entry per name). Manual readings are labelled as such where a regular-expression match was classified by hand. The acceptance-rate and summary-rejection lines rest on the journal's own statistics page, whose definitions (probabilities on average) differ from a simple share of decisions.

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Reproducibility checklist**: submissions without the completed checklist are desk rejected (Format; Data transparency requirement; https://jair.org/index.php/jair/about/submissions).
- **Format**: a submission not in the JAIR PDF format, for example a conference format, is rejected without review (Format).
- **Parallel submission**: a manuscript under review or published elsewhere is rejected with a six-month submission ban (Practical Concerns, Duplicate submission).
- **Required answers**: submissions whose three required answers are not clearly given will not be considered (Framing Requirements).
- **Surveys**: survey submissions are paused from 2026-12-01, with reopening planned for January 2027 (Format).
- No other hard blocker is supported by a fact I could read; ethics-approval rules and the open-access agreement text are unknown (Practical Concerns blanks).

### Soft Tax

- **Time**: the journal's own average is 42.0 weeks to acceptance, possibly after one revision (Review Cycle Time; https://jair.org/index.php/jair/transparent-publishing).
- **Selectivity**: overall acceptance probability 10.6% and 55.9% if not summarily rejected (Metrics); the journal says papers needing major revision are rejected with encouragement to resubmit, and a paper may be resubmitted only once (Peer Review).
- **Fit work**: the submission form requires naming 1 to 3 closest JAIR papers (Framing Requirements), which means reading the journal's output beforehand.
- **Format**: the journal moved to an ACM-based LaTeX format in spring 2025 (Format); conference-format files must be reworked.

### Best Suited For

- Methodological AI papers with experiments or proofs and reproducible code: `experiment` 31.4%, `theorem_proof_complexity` 13.2% of 592 abstracts, and the charter asks for reproducible experiments (Methodological Preferences).
- Work in constraint solving, planning, reinforcement learning, multi-agent systems and social choice: shares of 4.6% to 13.5% (Epistemological & Political Leanings).
- Authors who want no publication fee and open licensing: diamond open access with CC BY (Open Access).
- Fairness, bias and society-facing technical work: dedicated special tracks (Sensitive Topics).
- Extended versions of conference papers, which the journal accepts if declared (Framing Requirements).

### Not Recommended For

- Applications of known AI techniques without methodological insight: the journal lists these among the categories that usually face summary rejection (Framing Requirements).
- Qualitative or interview-based studies: `interview` matches 4 of 592 abstracts (Methodological Preferences). This shows rarity, not rejection.
- Authors who need a decision within three months: the stated target is 8 to 12 weeks, but the journal's own average to acceptance is 42.0 weeks (Review Cycle Time).
- Thesis chapters or conference papers rejected elsewhere without major improvement (Framing Requirements; transparent-publishing page).
